newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE CANOLA ENDS LOWER ON LONG LIQUIDATION, CBOT.
newsitem.headline: WCE CANOLA ENDS LOWER ON LONG LIQUIDATION, CBOT.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola futures ended down on long liquidation and a drop in CBOT soy complex futures ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Department of Agriculture production report.

"There's long liquidation of the August and the November. The trade's cautious ahead of the USDA report," a trader said. Sharply lower CBOT soybean values pressured canola but scale down commercial demand curbed losses.
CBOT soy tumbled Monday on much-needed weekend rains in the U.S. Midwest and forecasts for more through Tuesday.
November WCE canola crush profit margin fell to -19.87 Monday from -14.47 Friday. Nov-Jan spread at $4.30. Volume was 1,940 lot with 250 hedges.
August canola closed $2.60 lower at $354.60 and November ended down $3.10 at $357.
November flax lost $4.80 to settle at $290.20 on locals.
October western barley ended up $1.60 at $132.10, December up $1.80 to $134.20 on commission long liquidation with UGG the best buyer, traders said. Volume was 1,600 lots.
October feed wheat rose $0.40 to end at $155.20. XCan bought from UGG, traders said.
October feed peas fell US$1.20 to US$168.80 and December lost US$3.10 to close at $167.00. Volume was 50 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except oats, feed peas.)
